name: Persistent data structures
problem: Undo and concurrent readers need old versions to remain usable after an update.

origin.summary: Historical priority, inventor and first adoption remain unresolved. The cited primary documentation establishes the described mechanism, not its invention.

mechanism: An update returns a new collection value and can reuse unchanged immutable structure. Previous values retain their meanings; this is persistence across versions, not disk durability.
solutionFamily: Structural sharing versus full copy or in-place edit
costs: Extra indirection and retained versions consume memory.
Complexity depends on the chosen collection.
transferRule: Separate logical new versions from physical full copying.
confidence: MEDIUM: mechanism anchored to primary documentation; historical attribution and unknown language cells unresolved; traces are editorial reasoning examples.
examples: Clojure: v=[10 20]; w=(assoc v 1 99); reading v gives[10 20], w gives[10 99]. The API preserves v while implementation may share unchanged structure.
counterexamples: Immutability alone does not require structural sharing; a simple immutable implementation may copy everything.

assessment.prompt: Choose between persistent vectors and a copied array for frequent snapshots with sparse updates.
rubric: Compare allocation, lookup/update costs and version retention.
